title: Japan's Convenience Stores Launch AI-Designed Sweets
paragraphs: Would you like to try a lemon tart that tastes like pickles? It may sound strange, but it is one of several new sweets created with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) at Japanese convenience stores.

Two of Japan's biggest convenience store chains, Lawson and FamilyMart, have started using AI to come up with ideas for new food products. In both cases, AI was mainly used for brainstorming, while human food experts developed the final products.

Lawson's pickle-flavored lemon tart went on sale at the end of September at about 4,700 stores in the Kanto and Koshinetsu regions, which include Tokyo. The company also launched other AI-inspired items, including a bread roll filled with red bean paste, margarine and yogurt cream, and a Japanese-style salad served like a parfait. It is the first time Lawson has used AI to create and sell a product.

Interestingly, Lawson did not give the AI any information about past sales or market trends. Instead, it asked the AI to suggest unusual combinations. The company said it wanted ideas that were not limited by existing ways of thinking.

FamilyMart took a different approach. It gave the AI its sales data and asked it to suggest something new that would still sell well. The result was a French-style canelé made with sweet potato and caramel sauce. FamilyMart had already tested its first AI product, a biscuit sandwich filled with thick milk cream, in July. According to reports, the company plans to release ten more AI-designed products by January.

Customers seem curious about the new sweets. Shingo Shiina, 64, who tried the pickle tart, said it was a strange flavor but very tasty. Shiina added that a human would probably never have thought of it.
Still, some people wonder whether the trend is just a gimmick to attract attention, or whether AI will become a regular tool for creating new products.
